evidence.field: PDF p. 38, printed p. 26; 班 entry; scan pixels directly inspected
evidence.text: The 班 entry identifies the graph as 会意 and proposes that a knife divides jade, with the proposed original sense “divide auspicious jade.” Its form sequence is labeled Western Zhou (1), Spring and Autumn (2), Warring States (3), Shuowen small seal (4), Han (5), and regular script. The citation line matches those numbered forms: 1–2 cite 《金文编》 p. 26; 3 cites 《战文编》 p. 17; 4 cites 《说文》 p. 14; 5 cites 《篆隶表》 p. 26. I found no mismatch in the printed markers or bibliography, so the prior proposed OCR correction for this line is unsupported. The entry does not identify the two modern 王 shapes individually as 玨. The following supplied scan, PDF p. 39 (printed p. 27), has no continuation of the 班 entry. Edition: 2012 first edition, December; second printing July 2013; Tianjin Ancient Books Press and Liaoning People's Publishing House; ISBN 978-7-5528-0069-2. Scan: /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0038/source.png; source_pixel_sha256 b867d775afa82703d7dc56ef04623f8b078c28656162ac864f4b7d4ba9a1e6fc. PDF p. 39 scan: /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0039/source.png; source_pixel_sha256 c45db17ab0c4d4d5271e851b305454412c7ff1f2345c0383580eb95e250625e0. evidence.field: 班, A02566; 說文 forms and regular-script shape description
evidence.text: The official record distinguishes the Shuowen explanation and form from its regular-script description: it gives 分瑞玉 and analyzes the seal form as 玨 plus 刀; it says the regular-script form writes a slash and dot in the middle, describing these as a changed form of 刀. The record supports attributing the jade-and-knife analysis to the Shuowen tradition and relating the modern middle strokes to 刀. It does not say that each of the two visible 王 shapes independently represents 玨, nor does it independently establish that the earliest graph depicts the proposed action. It also gives Mandarin bān.

search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced the official MOE 班 entry. Opened it and checked the exact Shuowen component statement, regular-script shape description, pronunciation, and sense examples. Separately inspected the supplied full-size 字源 scans for PDF pp. 38–39; the sequence labels and citation line agree.

gaps: The book’s proposed knife-dividing-jade explanation is an attributed interpretation; the inspected passage does not independently establish that the earliest graph depicts that action.
The two outer modern 王 shapes should not be equated individually with historical 玨 on the basis of these passages; neither inspected source makes that specific mapping.
